evidence.text: Depicts a boat (舟) moving (止) forward (前).
不行而進謂之歬。从止在舟上。

Originally 歬, an ideogrammic compound (會意 /会意): 止 (“foot”) + 舟 (“boat”) – a foot on a boat moving forward.
In the current form, 止 is simplified to 䒑 and 舟 to 月. The current form with an additional 刀 (“knife”) (𠝣 > 𣦃 > 前) is the original form of 剪 (OC *ʔslenʔ, “to cut”).
Unrelated to 俞.
Unknown (Schuessler, 2007).

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: A00355-003 research note; variant relationship 歬/前
evidence.text: The entry treats 歬 as a variant of 前 and quotes Shuowen: 歬 means moving forward and is formed from 止 over 舟. It also records a competing traditional explanation: 刀+歬 was the graph for cutting evenly, later written 前 in clerical form; 歬 was then used for the directional word. Guangyun is cited as calling 歬 an old form of 前. This source reports competing historical lexicographic accounts; it does not resolve which graph was first.
evidence.title: A00355-003 歬 (前) - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.field: character evolution and cited inscription forms
evidence.text: The database lists 前 in bronze inscriptions (including bronze collection entries dated to Western Zhou) and in Shuowen small seal script. It describes 止 above 舟 as indicating a boat moving forward. This corroborates the graph components and a forward-motion interpretation in the bronze/seal record, but its page does not establish the earliest semantic stage or explain the separate 剪 analysis.
evidence.title: 漢字「前」：字形演變

evidence.source: 漢典 (ZDIC), quoting Shuowen and Duan Yucai's commentary
evidence.field: Shuowen entry for 歬 and commentary
evidence.text: The quoted Shuowen entry reads, in paraphrase, “moving forward is called 歬; formed from 止 on 舟.” Duan Yucai's note says later writers used 前, the graph associated with even cutting, for the directional word 歬, and used 翦 for cutting evenly. This explicitly distinguishes competing graph histories and a word/graph borrowing account; it supplies no independent pronunciation for a depicted tool or knife-name.
evidence.title: 前 qián、jiǎn - 汉典

evidence.text: The entry lists bronze forms, Chu manuscripts, Qin manuscripts, Shuowen seal form and Han clerical form; its visible bronze examples include Western Zhou middle and late inscriptions. It gives motion-forward as the basic verbal sense, cites 《广雅》 “前，进也,” and lists directional/front and earlier-in-time senses with citations such as 《诗·邶风·简兮》 and 《礼记·檀弓》. It also lists 前通翦 ‘cut/trim’ with a 《韩非子·八经》 citation. The page gives no securely dated earliest occurrence for each sense, and received-text citations are not themselves dated physical attestations.
evidence.title: 前 qián、jiǎn - 汉典

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 剪 entry, Shuowen graph analysis and sense
evidence.text: The entry quotes Shuowen's 剪 as “齊斷也。从刀，歬聲” (cut evenly; from 刀, with 歬 as phonetic). It says Shuowen wrote the cutting character as 前 and that the common modern graph is 剪. This supports 歬 as a sound component in this character according to Shuowen, but it does not establish the pronunciation/name of any depicted object in 前's graph.
evidence.title: A00364 剪 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.field: Kangxi citation on the cutting graph and written forms
evidence.text: The entry reports the 《正字通》 claim that 𠝣 is the original graph of 剪 and quotes Shuowen's analysis of the cutting graph as 刀 plus 歬 phonetic. It also reports the gloss ‘knife name’ in a Du Fu citation, but gives no historical reconstruction or evidence that a particular depicted implement was named with a sound matching 前. Thus a loan/graph-history theory about 前 and 剪 cannot be justified merely by reconstructing 前's pronoun or citing this later gloss.
evidence.title: 𠝣的解释|𠝣的意思|汉典“𠝣”字的基本解释

evidence.field: modern and historical readings of 前
evidence.text: The page gives modern Mandarin qián, Tang reading *dzhen, and Middle Chinese 昨先切, 從母, 先韻, 平聲, 四等, 開口. The Ministry dictionary and Shuowen-derived tradition conflict over whether 歬 (止 over 舟) is the original directional graph, or whether a graph with 刀 was the cutting word and 前 was borrowed for direction. The materials support reporting the disagreement, not resolving chronology.

The proposed relationship between the source word for ‘cut’ and any depicted tool/knife object remains under-evidenced. No independent original object name or pronunciation was recovered; a reconstruction of 前 alone would not prove that borrowing claim.

A direct Unihan lookup for 舟 (U+821F), 剪 (U+526A), and 歬 (U+6B6C) failed in the web tool. No component modern readings or full official record for these inspected entries are asserted. The supplied local dataset contains exact rows only for 前.

The supplied Baxter–Sagart row for 前 was checked, but no corresponding local Baxter–Sagart row for a proposed sound component was supplied or verified. No reconstructed phonetic comparison is claimed.

The currently verified attested meanings include forward motion, spatial ‘in front’, temporal ‘before/earlier’, guiding/leading, and reported graph/sense use for cutting. Their exact historical order and semantic transitions are not established by the available character-specific citations.
